findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP/22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the compromised host.

The user_data script exports a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plain text; anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or access to instance metadata can read these long-lived credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the legacy unauthenticated IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the web application could be used to steal instance credentials.
The instance is launched without root_block_device encryption settings, so the root EBS volume may store data unencrypted at rest.

The instance is placed in a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and routed directly to an internet gateway, giving it a public address and direct internet exposure rather than isolation in a private subnet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true or a KMS key, so attached data is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup data is also stored unencrypted and could be shared or restored without key controls.
The VPC flow log archive bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no SSE-KMS or customer-managed key), leaving sensitive network telemetry unencrypted by explicit configuration.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, ACL, or bucket policy restricts access to the flow log bucket, risking accidental public or cross-account exposure of network audit data.
The audit-log bucket has force_destroy = true and no versioning, MFA delete, or object lock, so flow log evidence can be deleted or tampered with silently.
There is no bucket policy denying non-HTTPS (aws:SecureTransport false) requests, so log data may be transmitted unencrypted in transit.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, exposing workloads that do not need inbound internet access.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP address, exposing workloads that do not need inbound internet access.

The VPC's default security group is never explicitly restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so it retains its permissive default allow-all-intra-group rules for any resource that inadvertently uses it.
